properties.name: Al Qantarah West
properties.role: Cairo-Port Said; Suez Canal west bank (Palestine link at Kantara)

properties.name: Damanhour
properties.notes: CANDIDATE: on the main-line corridor; not explicitly confirmed for the original line.

properties.name: El Cap
properties.notes: Location note: Historic canal-side station on the west-bank Ismailia/El Kantara-Port Said railway; by station order along the canal it sits between El Qantara West (to the south) and El Tina (to the north), roughly 13 km north of El Qantara West

properties.name: El Ferdan
properties.role: Canal-side station; El Ferdan swing bridge toward Sinai

properties.name: El Kantara (East)
properties.role: Sinai Military Railway start (east bank of the Suez Canal)

properties.name: El Tina
properties.notes: Location note: Historic canal-side station at the El Tina (El Tineh) plain near the southern approach to Port Said, where the Suez Canal nears the Mediterranean; on the west-bank Port Said railway, north of El Cap

properties.name: Nefisha
properties.notes: Location note: El Nefisha is the western district/suburb of Ismailia (~3-4 km SW of Ismailia city center); historically the Egyptian State Railways workshops site on the Cairo–Ismailia canal line. No precise station node located.

properties.name: Qalyub
properties.notes: CANDIDATE: on the main-line corridor; not explicitly confirmed for the original line.

properties.name: Qassasin
properties.notes: Location note: El Qassasin (Kassassin) is a town on the Cairo–Ismailia line in Sharqia, along the Sweet-Water (Ismailia) Canal between Tell el-Kebir (west) and Ismailia (east); site of the 1882 Battle of Kassassin. No sourced station coordinate obtained.

properties.name: Raswa
properties.notes: Location note: El Raswa is the southern approach to Port Said, where the railway/road cross the canal waterways (El Raswa bridges), ~3 km south of Port Said city center on the Ismailia–Port Said canal line.

properties.name: Romani
properties.notes: Location note: WWI Sinai station on the British standard-gauge military railway built east from El Qantara (on the Suez Canal). Romani lay ~23 mi (37 km) east of the canal and ~12 mi SW of Katia; Kantara–Romani–Katia line opened May 1916. Site of the Battle of Romani (Aug 1916). Estimate ~31.0,32.6 is consistent (near modern Rumana, coastal strip east of Qantara).

properties.name: Shellal
properties.role: Historic terminus; 1884 military line to Aswan
properties.notes: 1884 military line (first Sudan campaign); regauged to standard gauge 1926 (railwaywonders).

properties.name: Sidi Gaber
properties.notes: CANDIDATE: main-line stop, not confirmed on the original 1854-56 line.

properties.name: Tabiyet el-Agrud
properties.notes: Location note: Agrud (Ajrud) is a historic well/fort site NW of Suez on the Cairo–Suez desert line; 'Tabiyet el-Agrud' = the Agrud redoubt/battery. Estimate ~30.05,32.40 places it in the desert NW of Suez, toward the Bitter Lakes.

properties.name: Tanta
properties.notes: Described as the important junction between Alexandria and Cairo (railwaywonders).

properties.name: Rafah
properties.notes: Location note: Border station/railhead on the WWI British Kantara–Rafa (Sinai) military railway, which reached Rafah on the Egypt–Palestine frontier in early 1917 and later became the junction from which the branch to Beersheba was laid.; Rafa lies between Kantara East (Suez Canal) and Gaza on the coastal military line; Gaza is ~236 km from Kantara East, Rafa a little short of Gaza.

properties.name: Khanaqin
properties.notes: Location note: Branch terminus on the IRR Eastern line toward the Iranian border, in Diyala province; GeoNames has an entry for Khanaqin (id 94591) placing the town at roughly 34.35 N, 45.39 E, but the exact figure could not be read from a rendered page and the station point is not separately sourced.

properties.name: Kirkuk
properties.role: Baghdad-Kirkuk branch (not the Mosul-Baghdad main line)
properties.notes: Kirkuk lies on a separate branch; the Baghdad Railway main line runs Mosul-Baiji-Samarra-Baghdad.

properties.name: Elro'i
properties.notes: Location note: 'El Roi' station on the Jezreel Valley Railway, built 1945 (silicate-stone building), between Yagur (km 10.2 from Haifa) and Kiryat Haroshet (km 16.9 from Haifa). Near moshav Elro'i (Al Roy) south of Nesher.

properties.name: Kiryat Haroshet
properties.notes: Location note: Small cast-concrete Valley-railway halt at ~16.9 km from Haifa, by the Kishon, at the Kiryat Haroshet locality (part of Kiryat Tiv'on municipality). No precise station coordinate found.

properties.name: Nahariya
properties.role: HBT station; northern end of the surviving Israeli section

properties.name: Naharayim
properties.role: Added halt near the Jordan confluence
properties.notes: Location note: Halt near the Jordan-Yarmuk confluence at ~78.5 km on the Valley railway; the Naharayim power-station site is ~1 km east of kibbutz Gesher (International-Style building, 1937). No precise station coordinate found.

properties.name: Al-Sejed
properties.notes: Location note: Jaffa-Jerusalem-line station 'Al-Sejed (Ayn Sejed)' at 39.5 km from Jaffa, elevation 110.5-183 m, in use 1892-1915 only; lies between Ramla and Dayr Aban up the coastal-plain approach to the Judean foothills; Upline neighbour is Dayr Aban (Hartuv) at 50.3 km

properties.name: Bab al-Wad
properties.notes: NOT a station on the historic Jaffa-Jerusalem railway; Bab al-Wad is the road pass into the hills, not the railway’s Sorek-valley route.

properties.name: Latrun
properties.role: Ayalon-valley ROAD corridor (not on the 1892 railway)
properties.notes: NOT a station on the historic Jaffa-Jerusalem railway; Latrun is on the Ayalon road corridor / near the modern line, not the Sorek-valley alignment.

properties.name: Ghadir al-Hajj
properties.notes: Location note: Hejaz-line station south of Ma'an, on the section between Ma'an and Batn al-Ghul; Arab Revolt demolition site (British-Arab forces destroyed the track/bridges around Ghadir el Haj, spring 1918)

properties.name: Ma'an
properties.role: Junction: Hejaz trunk x Aqaba branch

properties.name: Ramtha
properties.role: Hejaz station near the Syrian border

properties.name: Shidiya
properties.notes: Location note: Esh-Shidiya (Eshidiya) phosphate-mine complex, a large open-pit area SE of Ma'an served by a branch line; historically a 'Bir Shidiya' watering stop existed on the Ma'an-to-Mudawwara section of the old Hejaz line, south of Ma'an

properties.name: Uneiza
properties.notes: Location note: 'Unayzah (Uneyze/Anaza) is a named populated place / station settlement in Ma'an Governorate, Jordan; Hejaz-line station at km 461 on the 1910 Ottoman State Year Book list (18 km before Wadi Rutm), in the Ma'an-to-Batn al-Ghoul desert sector

properties.name: Wadi Rutm
properties.notes:
Arabic should be وادي رتم (Wadi Rutm); the project list’s وادي رم is Wadi Rum, a different place.

Location note: Fortified Ottoman Hejaz station in the Batn al-Ghoul / Wadi Batn al-Ghoul area on the Fassu'ah Ridge descent, Ma'an Governorate; km 479 on the 1910 Ottoman State Year Book Hejaz list (18 km after Uneiza)

properties.name: Baalbek
properties.role: Rayak-Baalbek station (Roman ruins); km 26.8 from Rayak

properties.name: Beirut
properties.role: Coastal terminus (Mar Mikhael); rack climb begins

properties.name: Dahr el Baidar
properties.role: Summit of the line (Dar al-Baidar pass)

properties.name: Maalaka
properties.notes: Location note: Maalaka (El-Maallaqa) is the south-western quarter of Zahle; a 'Maalaqa station nearby Zahlé' is recorded in OSM; Beqaa station near Zahle on the Rayak line; our estimate sits ~1.5 km SW of Zahle center consistent with the El-Maallaqa quarter

properties.name: Yahfoufa
properties.notes: Location note: First station on the Beirut-Damascus metre-gauge rack line climbing east from Rayak toward Serghaya and the Syrian border; listed in station order between Riyak and Jisr el-Remman

properties.name: Akhdar
properties.notes: Location note: Official name 'Ahzar' / al-Akhdhar (Ottoman records); nicknamed 'Bughaz' (defile) by Turkish conscripts; two structures (main station + a separate water-supply 'Ahzar Alimentation'); ~km 798 from Haifa

properties.name: Al-Khanzira
properties.notes: Location note: Obscure Hejaz station, also called 'Al-Assda' (per our role note); no coordinate or dedicated page located

properties.name: Dahr al-Hajj
properties.role: Hejaz station S of Tabuk (Qareen al-Ghazal)
properties.notes: Location note: Hejaz station S of Tabuk; also known as 'SahrulGhul' / 'Khasm Birk' (per nabataea); role note calls it 'Qareen al-Ghazal'; ~km 782 from Haifa

properties.name: Medina
properties.role: Southern terminus of the Hejaz Railway

properties.name: Aleppo
properties.role: Baghdad Railway hub x DHP north junction

properties.name: Deraa
properties.role: Junction: Hejaz trunk x Haifa-Deraa branch

properties.name: El-Tekkieh
properties.notes: Location note: Barada-gorge DHP station 'El-Teqieh', listed in line order between Madaya and Souk Wadi Barada (i.e. in the gorge downstream of Madaya, upstream of Souq Wadi Barada); Downstream neighbour on the line; Further downstream gorge anchor

properties.name: Jisr el-Remman
properties.notes: Location note: DHP station 'Jisr el-Remman' (~1300 m altitude) at the summit end of the line, listed adjacent to Serghaya (1373 m) and Zabadani (1210 m) — i.e. in the Zabadani/Serghaya branch area; Neighbouring station on the summit section

properties.name: Serghaya
properties.role: Syrian summit-area railhead; ran into the 2000s

properties.name: Zabadani
properties.role: Resort station in the Barada valley

properties.name: Fevzipasa
properties.role: Amanus (Nur) Mts crossing; Ayran tunnel area

properties.name: Gaziantep
properties.role: On the MODERN Gaziantep-Karkamış reroute (bypasses Aleppo)
properties.notes: Not on the original Ottoman main line (Adana-Fevzipaşa-İslahiye-Meydan Ekbez-Aleppo); part of the later Turkish reroute bypassing Aleppo.

properties.name: Islahiye
properties.role: Baghdad Railway; ~22 km N of the Syrian border

properties.name: Konya
properties.role: Baghdad Railway start (from the Anatolian Rly)
